entries.subject: HST/STIS 0.58 micrometres, programmes 7125, 12551 and 12923, as reduced and deposited by Ren et al. (2023), VizieR J/A+A/672/A114
entries.finding: Clean down to 0.8 arcseconds (15.7 au), out to 82 au; orientation north up and east left, measured against the published position angle and the registered JWST images; midplane at 29.94 degrees. Drawn as the default lens.

entries.subject: JWST/NIRCam F210M and F410M behind MASK335R, 21 March 2025, programme 4758 observation c1002
entries.finding: MAST's level-3 mosaics, the star placed by planet b's orbit; clean from 2.5 arcseconds (49 au) to the field's edge at 126 au; midplane at 30.44 degrees.

entries.subject: Programme 4758 observation c1003, the second coronagraph visit of the same night
entries.finding: Pinned by archive.mts beside c1002 and not read: it images the same disc at the same wavelengths a few hours later, so it adds noise reduction, not coverage.
entries.revisitWhen: The disc lens needs lower noise at its outer edge.

entries.subject: JWST/NIRCam F182M behind MASK210R, 17 March 2023, programme 1411 observation c1011 (Rebollido et al. 2024)
entries.finding: MAST's automatic KLIP subtraction with one reference leaves speckle to about 1.5 arcseconds, and planet b is 2.7 times the scatter around it, so it reaches no closer than Hubble; the paper's own MCRDI reductions are not deposited. The programme's other five filters are level 2 only.
entries.revisitWhen: The authors deposit their reductions, or a reduction here beats MAST's inside 1.5 arcseconds.

entries.subject: JWST/MIRI F1550C and F2300C coronagraphy (programme 1411) and the thermal 'cat's tail'
entries.finding: MIRI's four-quadrant phase masks do not reproduce here (docs/jwst-imaging.md), so no MIRI coronagraph band is defined.
entries.revisitWhen: MIRI coronagraphy reproduces, or the authors deposit their images.

entries.subject: VLT/FORS V-band image of the outer disc (Janson et al. 2021), VizieR J/A+A/646/A132
entries.finding: A deposited 2048 x 2048 image reaching the disc's far reaches, beyond this volume's 170 au grid.
entries.revisitWhen: The volume is extended past 170 au.

entries.subject: HST/ACS/HRC F435W, F606W and F814W, programme 9987, starlight removed here with alpha Pictoris as the reference
entries.finding: Drawn as the colour lens, 29 to 135 au. The reference star is divided by the flux ratios Golimowski et al. (2006) state (1.65, 1.75, 1.90), and only the shift is fitted: 0.6 to 0.9 pixel against the paper's 0.8. A free fit would scale the reference 1.7 to 2.0 times higher, and far from the disc beta Pic's raw halo is 0.81 of alpha Pic's where the paper's ratio predicts 0.61, so about a quarter of the halo stays in the image. The paper's value is used because a published number outranks one fitted here; the free-fit scale is recorded in each product record.

entries.subject: How far the ACS colour lens is drawn
entries.finding: Drawn to the grid's edge, 135 au, though the images show the disc farther. Measured on the subtracted, roll-averaged images in 20 au bins along the midplane (within 6 au of it), in units of MJy/sr per Jy of starlight, against a per-channel noise of 0.0026 to 0.0035: 2.93 at 40-60 au, 1.18 at 80-100, 0.441 at 120-140, 0.249 at 140-160, 0.137 at 160-180, 0.084 at 180-200, 0.054 at 200-220, 0.036 at 220-240, 0.026 at 240-260, 0.018 at 260-280, 0.011 at 280-300 and 0.007 at 300-320, where the camera's field ends. Every lens of one bank must share a frame, so one grid holds all three; a grid wide enough for 320 au needs 4.1 au cells, and at that size the STIS lens's midplane cannot be measured (only 5 bins above five times the noise), so the wide grid was rejected. The lens states the cut in its recipe (beyondGrid) and the author keeps it as a limitation.
